forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

statement_nl: For integers b, m, and d with b >= 0, m >= 0, and d >= m, define F_{b,m,d}(q) := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(b+d+i)) / (1 - q^(b+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when m = 0. Assume that for every positive integer t one has floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t) <= floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t). Then F_{b,m,d}(q) lies in Z[q], and every coefficient in its standard expansion as a polynomial in q is a nonnegative integer.
